items.response:
Ugh, poor Hannah. The usual steps are to find out which impound lot the car went to (the city's towed-vehicle line or the police non-emergency number can tell her), then go with her ID, proof of ownership and insurance. The cost is normally the tow, daily storage and the ticket, but I don't want to quote figures from memory.
Action: Look up the current Toronto process and fees and send you a short summary to pass on to Hannah, and tell her to go soon since storage fees add up.

Good idea, a Zoom link is simpler for her than a freezing video call. I'll set it up for this week's call time and keep the text to her short and clear.
Action: Check your calendar for the call time, create the Zoom meeting for that slot, and text your mom the link with a one-line 'tap this at [time]' note. I'll show you the text first if you'd like.

Got it, short replies today.
Action: Keep everything to a couple of lines until you tell me otherwise.

Got it, short today.
Action: Keep replies to a line or two until 5.

Good to start early, since January isn't far off and passport timelines can slip. I'll build the checklist from the official Canada.ca page rather than from memory, so the requirements and fees are current.
Action: Pull the child passport renewal requirements into a checklist, check Leo's exact expiry date, and look for passport office appointment options near you, then send you everything.

Nice reason to celebrate. Since next Thursday is an office day on King West, I'll look nearby for a place that takes 8 and has a proper vegan main, so Wen is covered.
Action: Search restaurants near the King Street West office with group availability for 8 next Thursday and a real vegan main course, and send you two or three options before booking.

Here's the lemon loaf in grams (approximate):
- Flour 1 1/2 cups: about 190 g
- Sugar 1 cup: 200 g
- Butter 1/2 cup: 115 g
- Plain yogurt 1/2 cup: about 125 g
- Lemon juice 2 tbsp: about 30 g
- Baking powder 1 tsp: about 4 g
Action: Want me to save the metric version in your recipe notes?

I don't have Biscuit's birth date in front of me, so I won't guess it. I'd rather get it from his records than risk putting a wrong date on a vet form.
Action: Search your notes, emails and old vet or adoption records for his birth date, and draft behavioural notes if you tell me how he is with strangers, other dogs, the leash and loud noises.

That's lovely that she was so touched. I'll save it so I know for next year: your mom's birthday is November 3, and you send flowers through the Mumbai florist and call her that morning.
Action: Add a yearly reminder for Nov 3, with a note a week ahead to order the flowers, and I'll hold the Priya book order until you decide tonight.

Will do, all tentative. One thing to flag: Thursday 18 March is the anniversary of your dad's passing, and I know you like a lighter day around then.
Action: Add tentative holds for the deck due Fri 12 March, prep Mon 15 and Tue 16, and the offsite Wed 17 and Thu 18, and ask whether you'd like to leave Thursday evening free or talk to Tom about ending that day early.

On it. The pods and paper towels are household staples, so I'll reorder what you usually get. For the Dyson, I'll find options rather than buy, since it's a bigger purchase.
Action: Reorder the dishwasher pods and paper towels from your last order, then find a couple of cordless Dyson models, ask Hannah's model if you know it, and send you prices to choose from.

Sure. I'll open the instant payouts readiness doc and go through what's still open.
Action: Read the doc, list the unresolved comments, the linked Linear tickets and their status, and any items left over from the last review, then send you a short summary.

I don't want to put a guess in either form. I don't have your half marathon PB or the race in front of me, and I don't know how property tax is handled on your mortgage.
Action: Search your email and notes for your race results, and your mortgage documents for the property tax arrangement. I'll fill in what I can confirm and leave the rest blank for you to check.

Here's a quick version for Priya. Pros: better wellbeing and retention, a focus on output over hours, and a hiring edge. Cons: compressed days can get long, coverage and client expectations can get tricky, and some roles struggle to fit the work into four days.
Action: Send you a tidy two-column list to forward, and a few questions her firm should answer first, such as pay, coverage and a trial period.

October groceries were $972.55 across 16 transactions, the lowest of the three months. August was $1,108.42 and September was $1,346.29, which included a $312.44 Costco run on Sep 27.
Action: That's the three-month average of $1,142.42, so October was about $170 under. Want a store-by-store breakdown?
